item.title: Theory of relaxation and its effects on the electronic structure in twisted systems
item.description:
📚 Editors' Suggestions
👤 Junxi Yu, Bingbing Wang, and Cheng-Cheng Liu
Author(s): Junxi Yu, Bingbing Wang, and Cheng-Cheng Liu Here, the authors present an analytical and physically transparent theory of lattice relaxation in twisted systems. They show how the balance between intralayer elasticity and interlayer adhesion determines the relaxation pattern, and how this pattern can be analytically embedded into moiré electronic Hamiltonians. The work reveals how relaxation reshapes flat bands and shifts topological transitions toward experimentally relevant twist angles. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 245118] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026

item.description:

We explore how the dissipative geometric phase evolves within the spin-boson model, focusing specifically on coupling to an Ohmic bath in the weakly coherent regime. item.title: Design and prediction of a wide range sensor based on SPR-PCF for simultaneous measurement of temperature and magnetic field by Taguchi approach and machine learning
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Xiaozheng Jiang, Zhengrong Tong, Hao Wang, Weihua Zhang
A novel surface plasmon resonance–photonic crystal fiber (SPR-PCF) sensor is proposed for simultaneous measurement of temperature and magnetic field. The sensor is designed with two orthogonal polarized sensing channels filled with polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) and magnetic fluid (MF), respectively, which enables independent detection of temperature and magnetic field. Taguchi optimization method is employed to optimize the key structural parameters of the sensor. The proposed sensor is designed to operate over a wide temperature sensing range from − 20°C to 80°C, with a maximum sensitivity of 2.849 nm/°C. A magnetic field range of 0 to 50 mT is also covered, with a sensitivity of 1.42 nm/mT. Furthermore, multiple linear regression (MLR) and multilayer perceptron (MLP) machine learning mode…
